en: The Path of Discrimination 3:
The Chapter on Wisdom 3.1.
The Discourse on Great Wisdom
What wisdom is fulfilled by the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of impermanence?
What wisdom is fulfilled by the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of suffering?
What wisdom is fulfilled by the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of non-self? …pe…
When the contemplation of relinquishment is developed and cultivated, what kind of wisdom does it fulfill?
When the contemplation of impermanence is developed and cultivated, it fulfills swift wisdom.
When the contemplation of suffering is developed and cultivated, it fulfills penetrative wisdom.
The contemplation of non-self, when developed and cultivated, fulfills great wisdom.
The contemplation of disenchantment, when developed and cultivated, fulfills sharp wisdom.
The contemplation of dispassion, when developed and cultivated, fulfills vast wisdom.
The contemplation of cessation, when developed and cultivated, fulfills profound wisdom.
The contemplation of relinquishment, when developed and cultivated, fulfills peerless wisdom.
These seven kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill sagacity.
These eight kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill wide wisdom.
These nine kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill laughing wisdom.
Laughing wisdom is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.
Through the discernment of its meaning, the analytical knowledge of meaning (atthapaṭisambhidā) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the discernment of the phenomena, the analytical knowledge of phenomena (dhammapaṭisambhidā) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the discernment of the language, the analytical knowledge of language (niruttipaṭisambhidā) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the determination of inspired ingenuity, the analytical knowledge of inspired ingenuity (paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā) becomes attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Thus, these four analytical knowledges become attained, realized, and touched by his wisdom.
What wisdom does the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of impermanence regarding form fulfill? ... [and so on] ...
When the contemplation of relinquishment regarding form is developed and cultivated, what kind of wisdom does it fulfill?
When the contemplation of impermanence regarding form is developed and cultivated, it fulfills impulsive wisdom...
[and so on] ...when the contemplation of relinquishment regarding form is developed and cultivated, it fulfills peerless wisdom.
These seven kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill sagacity.
These eight kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill broad wisdom.
These nine kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill laughing wisdom.
The analytical knowledge of perspicuity is the analytical knowledge of eloquence.
Through the discernment of its meaning, the analytical knowledge of meaning is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the discernment of the phenomena, the analytical knowledge of phenomena is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the determination of language, the analytical knowledge of language (nirutti-paṭisambhidā) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the determination of ingenuity, the analytical knowledge of ingenuity (paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Thus, these four analytical knowledges are attained, realized, and touched by his wisdom.
In feeling … pe … in perception … in mental formations …

When the contemplation of impermanence has been developed and cultivated with respect to consciousness … the eye … [and so on] … with respect to aging-and-death, what kind of wisdom does it fulfill? … [as before] …
When the contemplation of relinquishment regarding aging and death is developed and cultivated, what kind of wisdom does it fulfill?
When the contemplation of impermanence regarding aging and death is developed and cultivated,
it fulfills impulsive wisdom … [and so on] … when the contemplation of relinquishment regarding aging and death is developed and cultivated, it fulfills peerless wisdom.
These seven kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill sagacity.
These eight kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill vast wisdom.
These nine kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill joyous wisdom.
The analytical knowledge of perspicuity is the analytical knowledge of eloquence.
Through the discernment of its meaning, the analytical knowledge of meaning is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the discernment of the phenomena, the analytical knowledge of phenomena is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the determination of language, the analytical knowledge of language (nirutti-paṭisambhidā) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the determination of ingenuity, the analytical knowledge of ingenuity (paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Thus, these four analytical knowledges are attained, realized, and touched by his wisdom.
When the contemplation of impermanence regarding forms is developed and cultivated, what kind of wisdom does it fulfill?
When the contemplation of impermanence regarding past, future, and present forms is developed and cultivated, what kind of wisdom does it fulfill?
When the contemplation of suffering regarding forms is developed and cultivated, what kind of wisdom does it fulfill?
What wisdom is fulfilled by the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of suffering regarding past, future, and present form?
What wisdom is fulfilled by the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of non-self regarding form?
What wisdom is fulfilled by the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of non-self regarding past, future, and present form?
The contemplation of disenchantment with form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills what kind of wisdom?
The contemplation of disenchantment with past, future, and present forms, when developed and cultivated, fulfills what kind of wisdom?
The contemplation of dispassion toward form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills what kind of wisdom?
What wisdom is fulfilled by the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of dispassion regarding past, future, and present forms?
What wisdom is fulfilled by the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of cessation regarding forms?
What wisdom is fulfilled by the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of cessation regarding past, future, and present forms?
What wisdom is fulfilled by the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of relinquishment regarding forms?
What wisdom is fulfilled by the cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of relinquishment regarding past, future, and present forms?
The cultivation and frequent practice of the contemplation of impermanence regarding forms fulfills impulsive wisdom (*javanapaññā*).
The contemplation of impermanence regarding past, future, and present form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills impulsive wisdom.
The contemplation of suffering regarding form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills penetrative wisdom.
The contemplation of suffering regarding past, future, and present form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills impulsive wisdom.
The contemplation of non-self regarding form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills great wisdom.
The contemplation of non-self regarding past, future, and present forms, when developed and cultivated, fulfills swift wisdom.
The contemplation of disenchantment regarding form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills sharp wisdom.
The contemplation of disenchantment with respect to past, future, and present form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills impulsive wisdom.
The contemplation of dispassion with respect to form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills vast wisdom.
The contemplation of dispassion with respect to past, future, and present form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills impulsive wisdom.
The contemplation of cessation regarding form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills profound wisdom.
The contemplation of cessation regarding past, future, and present forms, when developed and cultivated, fulfills swift wisdom.
The contemplation of relinquishment regarding form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills peerless wisdom.
The contemplation of relinquishment regarding past, future, and present form, when developed and cultivated, fulfills impulsive wisdom.
These seven kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill sagacity.
These eight kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill vast wisdom.
These nine kinds of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the wisdom of wit.
The wisdom of wit is the analytical knowledge of expression (*paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā*).
Through the determination of its meaning, the analytical knowledge of meaning (*attha-paṭisambhidā*) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the discernment of phenomena, the analytical knowledge of phenomena (dhamma-paṭisambhidā) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the discernment of language, the analytical knowledge of language (nirutti-paṭisambhidā) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Through the discernment of ingenuity, the analytical knowledge of ingenuity (paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom.
For him, these four analytical insights (paṭisambhidā) have been attained, realized, and touched by means of wisdom.
[The same applies to] feeling … perception … [and so on].
In volitional formations … in consciousness … in the eye … [and so on] … up to … [the six sense bases] … in aging-and-death.
When the contemplation of impermanence regarding aging and death is developed and cultivated, what kind of wisdom does it fulfill?
When the contemplation of impermanence regarding past, future, and present aging and death is developed and cultivated, what kind of wisdom does it fulfill?
…pe… When the contemplation of relinquishment regarding aging and death is developed and cultivated, what kind of wisdom does it fulfill?
When the contemplation of relinquishment regarding past, future, and present aging-and-death is developed and cultivated, what kind of wisdom does it fulfill?
When the contemplation of impermanence regarding aging-and-death is developed and cultivated, it fulfills impulsive wisdom.
When the contemplation of impermanence regarding past, future, and present aging-and-death is developed and cultivated, it fulfills impulsive wisdom... [and so on].
In him, these four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) have been attained, realized, and touched by means of wisdom.
“Monks, these four things, when developed and cultivated, lead to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry.
What are the four?”

"Association with superior persons, hearing the true Dhamma, careful attention, and practice in accordance with the Dhamma—these four things, monks, when developed and cultivated, lead to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry.
These four things, monks, when developed and cultivated, lead to the realization of the fruit of once-returning... [and so on].
They lead to the realization of the fruit of non-returning …pe… they lead to the realization of the fruit of arhatship.
Which four?

"Association with superior persons, hearing the true Dhamma, wise attention, and practice in accordance with the Dhamma—these four things, monks, when developed and cultivated, lead to the realization of the fruit of the path of arahantship.
These four things, monks, when developed and cultivated, lead to the acquisition of wisdom... [and so on].
They lead to the development of wisdom, they lead to the expansion of wisdom,
they lead to great wisdom, they lead to broad wisdom, they lead to vast wisdom, they lead to deep wisdom,
they lead to peerless wisdom, they lead to abundant wisdom, and they lead to an abundance of wisdom.
They conduce to swiftness of wisdom, they conduce to lightness of wisdom, they conduce to joyousness of wisdom,
they conduce to fleetness of wisdom, they conduce to sharpness of wisdom, and they conduce to penetrative wisdom. Which four?
“Association with superior persons, hearing the true Dhamma, careful attention, and practice in accordance with the Dhamma—
these four things, bhikkhus, when developed and cultivated, lead to the acquisition of wisdom,
lead to the increase of wisdom, and lead to penetrative wisdom.”
3.1.1. Exposition of the Sixteen Kinds of Wisdom Regarding the phrase "they conduce to the acquisition of wisdom": what is the acquisition of wisdom?
It is the four kinds of knowledge of the paths, the four kinds of knowledge of the fruits, the four kinds of analytical knowledge, and the six...
The gain, acquisition, attainment, achievement, contact, realization, and fulfillment of the superknowledges, of the seventy-three knowledges, and of the seventy-seven knowledges.
They lead to the acquisition of wisdom— thus it is said.
This is the acquisition of wisdom.
Regarding the phrase "it leads to the growth of wisdom," what is the growth of wisdom?
The wisdom of the seven types of trainees (*sekha*) and of the virtuous worldling (*puthujjanakalyāṇaka*) increases; the wisdom of the arahant increases.
"Insight and intelligence lead to further increase"—
this is insight and intelligence.
"They lead to the expansion of wisdom"— what is the expansion of wisdom?
The wisdom of the seven trainees and of the virtuous worldling reaches abundance.
For the Arahant, wisdom has already reached abundance; thus, it conduces to the further abundance of wisdom.
This is the abundance of wisdom.
“They lead to great wisdom”: what is great wisdom?
It grasps great meanings—thus it is great wisdom.
It grasps great phenomena—thus it is great wisdom.
She comprehends great modes of expression; thus she is one of great wisdom.
She comprehends great flashes of ingenuity; thus she is one of great wisdom.
She comprehends the great aggregate of virtue; thus she is one of great wisdom.
She grasps the great aggregate of concentration;
thus she is one of great wisdom. She grasps the great aggregate of wisdom; thus she is one of great wisdom.
She grasps the great aggregate of liberation; thus she is one of great wisdom.
She comprehends the great aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation; thus she is one of great wisdom.
She comprehends the great points of what is possible and what is impossible; thus she is one of great wisdom.
She comprehends the great meditative abidings and attainments; thus she is one of great wisdom.
She comprehends the great noble truths, thus she is one of great wisdom.
She comprehends the great foundations of mindfulness, thus she is one of great wisdom.
She comprehends the great right endeavors, thus she is one of great wisdom.
She grasps the great bases of psychic power; thus she is one of great wisdom.
She grasps the great faculties; thus she is one of great wisdom.
She grasps the great powers; thus she is one of great wisdom.
She grasps the great factors of enlightenment, thus she is one of great wisdom.
She grasps the great noble path, thus she is one of great wisdom.
She grasps the great fruits of recluseship, thus she is one of great wisdom.
She grasps the great direct knowledges, thus she is one of great wisdom.
She grasps the great ultimate truth, Nibbāna, thus she is one of great wisdom.
They lead to the state of great wisdom, thus...
This is great wisdom.
Regarding the statement, "It leads to broad wisdom," what is broad wisdom?
Knowledge that occurs with respect to various and diverse aggregates is broad wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding diverse and various elements is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding diverse and various bases is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding diverse and various dependent originations is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that proceeds regarding the non-apprehension of emptiness as diverse and manifold is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that proceeds regarding meanings as diverse and manifold is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that proceeds regarding phenomena as diverse and manifold is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding various and diverse expressions is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding various and diverse repartees is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding various and diverse aggregates of virtue is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the various and diverse aggregates of concentration is "wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the various and diverse aggregates of wisdom is "wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the various and diverse aggregates of liberation is "wide wisdom."
Knowledge that occurs regarding the various and diverse aggregates of liberation and vision is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding various and diverse bases and non-bases is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding various and diverse abidings and attainments is wide wisdom.
Knowledge occurs regarding the various and diverse noble truths—this is wide wisdom.
Knowledge occurs regarding the various and diverse foundations of mindfulness—this is wide wisdom.
Knowledge occurs regarding the various and diverse right endeavors—this is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the various and diverse bases of psychic power is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the various and diverse faculties is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the various and diverse powers is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the various and diverse factors of enlightenment is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the various and diverse noble paths is wide wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the various and diverse fruits of recluseship is wide wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding various and diverse direct knowledges (abhiññā); thus, it is "wide wisdom" (puthupaññā).
Knowledge proceeds having transcended the states shared by worldlings (puthujjana) and reached the ultimate truth of Nibbāna;
thus, it is "wide wisdom. They lead to the state of wide wisdom.
This is broad wisdom.
What is expansive wisdom, since it leads to expansiveness of wisdom?
It grasps extensive meanings, thus it is expansive wisdom.
One comprehends vast phenomena; thus, it is "vast wisdom.
One comprehends vast linguistic expressions; thus, it is "vast wisdom.
One comprehends vast inspired insights; thus, it is "vast wisdom."
One who comprehends the vast aggregate of virtue possesses vast wisdom.
One who comprehends the vast aggregate of concentration possesses vast wisdom.
One who comprehends the vast aggregate of wisdom possesses vast wisdom.
She grasps the vast aggregate of liberation; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
She grasps the vast aggregate of knowledge and vision of liberation; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
She grasps the vast grounds and non-grounds; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
She comprehends the vast dwellings and attainments; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
She comprehends the vast noble truths; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
She comprehends the vast foundations of mindfulness; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
One comprehends the vast right efforts—thus it is "vast wisdom.
One comprehends the vast bases of psychic power—thus it is "vast wisdom.
One comprehends the vast faculties—thus it is "vast wisdom."
She grasps vast powers; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
She grasps the vast factors of enlightenment; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
She grasps the vast Noble Path; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
She grasps the vast fruits of recluseship; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
She grasps the vast direct knowledges; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
She grasps the vast ultimate truth, Nibbāna; thus she is one of vast wisdom.
"They lead to vast wisdom"—
this is vast wisdom.
"They lead to profound wisdom"— what is profound wisdom?
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound aggregates; thus it is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound elements; thus it is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound sense bases; thus it is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound dependent origination—this is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound emptiness and non-apprehension—this is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding profound meanings—this is profound wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding profound phenomena is profound wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding profound expressions is profound wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding profound insights is profound wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the profound aggregate of virtue is profound wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the profound aggregate of concentration is profound wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the profound aggregate of wisdom is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound aggregates of liberation; thus it is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound aggregates of knowledge and vision of liberation; thus it is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound points of possibility and impossibility; thus it is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound dwellings and attainments—this is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound Noble Truths—this is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound foundations of mindfulness—this is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound right efforts; thus it is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound bases of psychic power; thus it is profound wisdom.
Knowledge proceeds regarding the profound faculties; thus it is profound wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the profound powers is profound wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the profound factors of enlightenment is profound wisdom.
Knowledge that occurs regarding the profound noble path is profound wisdom.
Knowledge occurs regarding the profound fruits of recluseship: thus it is profound wisdom.
Knowledge occurs regarding the profound direct knowledges: thus it is profound wisdom.
Knowledge occurs regarding the profound ultimate truth, Nibbāna: thus it is profound wisdom.
"Leading to profound wisdom"—
this is profound wisdom.
"Leading to peerless wisdom"— what is peerless wisdom?
In that person for whom the analytical knowledge of meaning has been attained, realized, and touched by wisdom through the discernment of meaning;
for whom the analytical knowledge of phenomena has been attained, realized, and touched by wisdom through the discernment of phenomena;
and for whom the analytical knowledge of language has been attained, realized, and touched [by wisdom] through the discernment of language.
Through wisdom, by way of the determination of inspired eloquence, the analytical knowledge of inspired eloquence (*paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā*) is attained, realized, and touched by wisdom;
regarding his meaning, phenomena, language, and inspired eloquence, no one else is able to equal him.
And he is not to be equaled by others—thus it is said.
One of non-adjacent wisdom.
The wisdom of a virtuous worldling is distant, very distant, far distant from the wisdom of one who has entered the eighth stage; it is neither near nor adjacent.
Compared to the virtuous worldling, the one who has entered the eighth stage possesses non-adjacent wisdom.
The wisdom of one at the eighth stage is distant, very distant, extremely distant from the wisdom of a stream-enterer; it is neither near nor proximate.
Compared to the one at the eighth stage, the stream-enterer possesses incomparable wisdom.
The wisdom of a stream-enterer is distant, very distant, extremely distant from the wisdom of a once-returner; it is neither near nor proximate.
Compared to the stream-enterer, the once-returner possesses wisdom that is not proximate;
the wisdom of the once-returner is distant, very distant, extremely distant from the wisdom of the non-returner—it is neither near nor proximate.
Compared to the once-returner, the non-returner possesses wisdom that is not proximate.
The wisdom of a non-returner is far, very far, and extremely far from the wisdom of an arahant; it is neither near nor proximate.
Compared to a non-returner, an arahant possesses incomparable wisdom.
The wisdom of an arahant is far, very far, and extremely far from the wisdom of a paccekabuddha; it is neither near nor proximate.
Compared to an Arahant, a Paccekabuddha possesses peerless wisdom.
Compared to both a Paccekabuddha and the world with its devas, a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, is supreme and possesses peerless wisdom.

He is skilled in the analysis of wisdom, possessed of penetrating knowledge, attained to the analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā), endowed with the four grounds of self-confidence, and the bearer of the ten powers.
A bull among men, a lion among men, an elephant among men, a noble steed among men, a stallion among men; one of infinite knowledge, infinite power, and infinite fame;

wealthy, possessing great riches, and possessed of wealth; a leader, a trainer, an inspirer, one who makes known, one who causes to perceive, one who causes to behold, and one who inspires confidence.
For that Blessed One is the arouser of the unarisen path, the producer of the unproduced path, and the proclaimer of the unproclaimed path.
“He is the proclaimer of the path, the knower of the path, the discoverer of the path, the one skilled in the path; and his disciples now dwell following that path, having subsequently attained it.

For the Blessed One knows what should be known and sees what should be seen; he has become the eye, become wisdom, become the Dhamma, become the Brahma; he is the speaker, the one who sets things in motion, the guide to the goal, the giver of the Deathless, the Lord of the Dhamma, the Tathāgata.
There is nothing unknown, unseen, uncomprehended, unrealized, or untouched by wisdom for that Blessed One.
With respect to the past, the future, and the present, all phenomena in every aspect come within the range of the Buddha, the Blessed One’s, sphere of knowledge.
Whatever is knowable, all that must be known.
Whether it be for one’s own benefit, for the benefit of others, or for the benefit of both; whether it be a benefit pertaining to the present life or a benefit pertaining to future lives;
whether it be a benefit that is shallow or a benefit that is profound; whether it be a benefit that is hidden or a benefit that is concealed;

whether it be a benefit that requires further interpretation or a benefit that is definitive; whether it be a benefit that is blameless, a benefit that is free from defilement, a benefit that is purified, or the ultimate benefit.
Whatever purpose there may be, all of it revolves within the Buddha’s knowledge.
Every bodily action of the Buddha, the Blessed One, conforms to his knowledge.
Every verbal action of the Buddha, the Blessed One, conforms to his knowledge.
All mental action of the Buddha, the Blessed One, proceeds in accordance with his knowledge.
The Buddha, the Blessed One’s, knowledge regarding the past is unobstructed.
The Buddha, the Blessed One’s, knowledge regarding the future is unobstructed.
Regarding the present, the knowledge of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is unimpeded.
To the extent that there is an object to be known, to that extent is there knowledge; to the extent that there is knowledge, to that extent is there an object to be known.
Knowledge has the object to be known as its limit; the object to be known has knowledge as its limit.
Knowledge does not proceed beyond the knowable;
there is no path of the knowable beyond knowledge.
These phenomena exist as mutually defined limits.

Just as when two caskets are perfectly joined together, the lower casket does not overstep the upper one, and the upper casket does not overstep the lower one, but they stand with their limits meeting one another;
even so, for the Buddha, the Blessed One, the range of what is to be known (*neyya*) and his knowledge (*ñāṇa*) stand with their limits meeting one another.
As far as there is the range of what is to be known, so far is there knowledge; as far as there is knowledge, so far is the range of what is to be known.
Knowledge has the knowable as its limit; the knowable has knowledge as its limit.
Knowledge does not proceed beyond the knowable;
there is no path of the knowable beyond knowledge.
Those phenomena exist with one another as their limit.
The knowledge of the Buddha, the Blessed One, operates regarding all phenomena.
All phenomena are dependent upon the advertence, the desire, the attention, and the arising of consciousness of the Buddha, the Blessed One.
The knowledge of the Buddha, the Blessed One, operates toward all beings.
The Buddha knows the disposition of all beings, he knows their underlying tendencies, he knows their conduct, and he knows their inclinations.

He discerns beings who have little dust in their eyes and those with much dust in their eyes; those with sharp faculties and those with dull faculties; those of good character and those of bad character; those easy to instruct and those difficult to instruct; and those who are capable and those who are incapable.
The world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans, revolves within the Buddha’s knowledge.
Just as whatever fish and turtles there are, including even the great timiṅgala, revolve within the great ocean,
even so the world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans, revolves within the Buddha’s knowledge.
Just as whatever winged creatures there may be, even including the garuḍa, the son of Vinatā, move only within a portion of space;
even so, those who are equal to Sāriputta in wisdom move only within a portion of the Buddha’s knowledge.
The Buddha’s knowledge stands having pervaded and surpassed the wisdom of gods and humans.
Furthermore, those wise khattiyas, wise brahmins, wise householders, and wise recluses— clever, skilled in the doctrines of others,
like hair-splitting archers who move as if piercing through with the shaft of their wisdom— their various speculative views— they formulate question after question and,
having approached the Tathāgata, ask him about things that are hidden and concealed.
“Those questions you asked have been answered by the Blessed One and their reasons have been demonstrated.
They have been successfully resolved for the Blessed One.
Thus, the Blessed One outshines them all in wisdom.”
"Supreme with peerless wisdom; they lead to peerless wisdom"—this is peerless wisdom.
"They lead to vast wisdom": what is vast wisdom?
One who overcomes lust is one of vast wisdom.
One who has overcome it is one of vast wisdom.
One who overcomes hatred is one of vast wisdom.
She is called "one of vast wisdom" because she has overcome [all things].
She is called "one of vast wisdom" because she has overcome delusion.
She is called "one of vast wisdom" because she has overcome.
Anger … ill will … disparagement …
...vanity... envy...
stinginess...
Deceit … guile … obstinacy …
...aggression ...
conceit ...
overweening pride...
Arrogance … negligence … all defilements …
One who overcomes all misconduct … all volitional formations … [and so on] … all kamma leading to existence is one of vast wisdom.
"Overcome"—thus she is one of vast wisdom.
"Lust is an enemy; she has wisdom that crushes that enemy"—thus she is one of vast wisdom.
"Hatred is an enemy; she has wisdom that crushes that enemy"—thus she is one of vast wisdom.
Delusion is an enemy; wisdom that crushes that enemy is "vast wisdom.
Anger... [and so on] ...resentment... [and so on].
Deceit … hypocrisy … envy …
Avarice … deceit … craftiness …
Arrogance … hostility … conceit …
excessive pride … intoxication … negligence …
All defilements … all misconducts … all volitional formations … [and so on] …
All kamma leading to existence is overcome by that noble wisdom which crushes the ignoble; thus she is "of vast wisdom" (bhūripaññā).
"Vast" (bhūri) is said to be the earth.
One who is endowed with wisdom that is as extensive and abundant as the earth is "of vast wisdom."
Moreover, this is a designation for wisdom:
"vast intelligence, guiding"—that is, vast wisdom.
They lead to the state of having vast wisdom.
This is vast wisdom.
Regarding the phrase "leading to an abundance of wisdom," what is meant by an abundance of wisdom?
Here, a certain person is one for whom wisdom is heavy, who conducts himself according to wisdom, who seeks wisdom, who is intent upon wisdom, whose banner is wisdom, and whose standard is wisdom.

One who has wisdom as the dominant influence, who abounds in investigation, abounds in close investigation, abounds in scrutiny, abounds in thorough scrutiny, whose nature is to scrutinize thoroughly, who dwells in clarity, who is devoted to that,
who makes that his weight, who abounds in that, who is inclined toward that, who leans toward that, who tends toward that, who is intent upon that, and who has that as the dominant influence—

just as one who makes a group his weight is called "one who abounds in groups," one who makes robes his weight is called "one who abounds in robes," one who makes a bowl his weight is called "one who abounds in bowls," and one who makes lodgings his weight is called "one who abounds in lodgings."
In the same way, here someone is one for whom wisdom is heavy, who conducts himself with wisdom, whose aim is wisdom, who is intent on wisdom,

whose banner is wisdom, whose standard is wisdom, who has wisdom as his sovereign; he is full of investigation, full of scrutiny, full of looking down, full of looking around, having the nature of looking all around,
dwelling in clarity, conducting himself according to that, making that his burden, abounding in that, inclining toward that, leaning toward that.
Inclined toward that, intent upon that, dominated by that.
"They conduce to an abundance of wisdom"—
this is the abundance of wisdom.
“They conduce to swiftness of wisdom”: what is swiftness of wisdom?
One fulfills the precepts very swiftly—this is swiftness of wisdom.
One fulfills restraint of the sense faculties very swiftly—this is swiftness of wisdom.
One who very quickly fulfills moderation in eating is one of swift wisdom;
one who very quickly fulfills devotion to wakefulness is one of swift wisdom;
one who very quickly fulfills the aggregate of virtue is one of swift wisdom.
It quickly, very quickly, fulfills the aggregate of concentration;
thus it is "swift wisdom. It quickly, very quickly, fulfills the aggregate of wisdom; thus it is "swift wisdom.
It quickly, very quickly, fulfills the aggregate of liberation; thus it is "swift wisdom."
It quickly, very quickly, fulfills the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation—this is swift wisdom.
It quickly, very quickly, penetrates what is possible and what is impossible—this is swift wisdom.
It quickly, very quickly, fulfills the dwellings and attainments—this is swift wisdom.
One who penetrates the noble truths very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who develops the foundations of mindfulness very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who develops the right efforts very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who develops the bases of psychic power very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who develops the faculties very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who develops the powers very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who develops the factors of enlightenment very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who develops the noble path very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who realizes the fruits of recluseship very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
“One penetrates the direct knowledges very quickly, very quickly”—this is quick wisdom.
“One realizes the ultimate goal, Nibbāna, very quickly, very quickly”—this is quick wisdom.
“They lead to the state of quick wisdom”—thus it is said.
This is swift wisdom.
What is fleet wisdom, which leads to fleetness of wisdom?
One fulfills the precepts very swiftly—this is fleet wisdom.
Because one quickly, very quickly, fulfills restraint of the sense faculties, it is "swift wisdom.
Because one quickly, very quickly, fulfills moderation in eating, it is "swift wisdom.
Because one quickly, very quickly, fulfills devotion to wakefulness, it is "swift wisdom."
Very quickly [he masters] the aggregate of virtue … the aggregate of concentration … the aggregate of wisdom …
One fulfills the aggregate of liberation … the aggregate of knowledge and vision of liberation— this is quick wisdom.
One penetrates very quickly what is possible and what is impossible— this is quick wisdom.
One quickly and easily fulfills the dwellings and attainments—this is quick wisdom.
One quickly and easily penetrates the noble truths—this is quick wisdom.
One quickly and easily develops the foundations of mindfulness—this is quick wisdom.
One who develops the right efforts very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who develops the bases of psychic power very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who develops the faculties very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
"One who develops the powers quickly, quickly" is quick wisdom.
"One who develops the factors of enlightenment quickly, quickly" is quick wisdom.
"One who develops the noble path quickly, quickly" is quick wisdom.
One who realizes the fruits of recluseship very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who penetrates the higher knowledges very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
One who realizes the ultimate goal, Nibbāna, very quickly is one of quick wisdom.
“They conduce to buoyant wisdom”—
this is buoyant wisdom.
“They conduce to laughing wisdom”— what is laughing wisdom?
Here, someone who abounds in laughter, abounds in joy, abounds in contentment, and abounds in gladness fulfills the precepts—this is "laughter-wisdom" (*hāsapaññā*).
One who abounds in laughter, abounds in joy, abounds in contentment, and abounds in gladness fulfills restraint of the sense faculties—this is "laughter-wisdom.
One who abounds in laughter, abounds in joy, abounds in contentment, and abounds in gladness fulfills moderation in eating—this is "laughter-wisdom."

One who abounds in laughter, abounds in rapture, abounds in satisfaction, and abounds in gladness fulfills the practice of wakefulness— this is laughter-wisdom (*hāsapaññā*). One who abounds in laughter,
abounds in rapture, abounds in satisfaction, and abounds in gladness [fulfills] the aggregate of virtue (*sīlakkhandha*) …pe… the aggregate of concentration (*samādhikkhandha*) … [and so on].
He fulfills the aggregate of wisdom … the aggregate of liberation … the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation … [and so on] …
He penetrates what is possible and what is impossible;
he fulfills the dwellings and attainments;
he penetrates the noble truths.
"He develops the foundations of mindfulness" ...
"he develops the right efforts" ...
"he develops the bases of psychic power" ...
"One develops the faculties," ...
"one develops the powers," ...
"one develops the factors of enlightenment."
"One develops the noble path" ...
"one realizes the fruits of recluseship"—this is joyous wisdom (*hāsapaññā*).
"Abounding in joy, abounding in rapture, abounding in contentment, abounding in gladness, one penetrates the direct knowledges"—this is joyous wisdom.
One who abounds in laughter, abounds in knowledge, abounds in contentment, and abounds in gladness realizes the ultimate goal, Nibbāna;
thus it is "laughter-wisdom" (hāsapaññā). That which leads to the state of laughter-wisdom is called "laughter-wisdom."
“They conduce to fleetness of wisdom”: what is fleetness of wisdom?
Whatever form there is—past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior;
far or near—all form one fleetly understands as impermanent: this is fleetness of wisdom.
It rushes swiftly toward [the perception of] suffering—this is impulsive wisdom.
It rushes swiftly toward [the perception of] non-self—this is impulsive wisdom. Whatever feeling there may be... [and so on].
Whatever perception there is … whatever formations there are … whatever consciousness there is—whether past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle—
Whether inferior or superior, far or near—all consciousness it swiftly impels as impermanent; thus it is "swift wisdom.
It swiftly impels [it] as suffering; thus it is "swift wisdom.
It swiftly impels [it] as non-self; thus it is "swift wisdom."
The eye … [and so on] … aging-and-death, whether past, future, or present, is swiftly impelled as impermanent— this is impelling wisdom.
It is swiftly impelled as suffering— this is impelling wisdom.
It speeds swiftly toward [the realization of] non-self, thus it is "swift wisdom" (javanapaññā).

Having weighed, scrutinized, discerned, and made manifest that form—past, future, and present—is impermanent in the sense of destruction, suffering in the sense of terror, and non-self in the sense of being coreless, it speeds swiftly toward the cessation of form, which is Nibbāna; thus it is "swift wisdom."
Feeling … perception … volitional formations …
Consciousness … the eye … and so on … aging-and-death, whether past, future, or present, is impermanent in the sense of destruction, suffering in the sense of terror, and non-self.
"In the sense of being pithless": having weighed, scrutinized, analyzed, and made clear that it is pithless, one swiftly rushes toward Nibbāna, which is the cessation of aging and death;
thus it is "swift wisdom" (*javanapaññā*).
Form—past, future, and present—is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, and subject to vanishing.

Having weighed, having scrutinized, having clarified, and having made manifest that form is subject to dispassion and subject to cessation, one swiftly impels toward the cessation of form, which is Nibbāna;
this is impulsive wisdom (*javanapaññā*). [The same applies to] feeling …pe… [and so on].
Perception … volitional formations … consciousness …

Having weighed, scrutinized, and clearly understood that the eye— and so on, up to— aging and death, whether past, future, or present, are impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction,
subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, and subject to cessation; having made them clear.
Having done so, it swiftly speeds toward Nibbāna, which is the cessation of aging and death;
thus it is "swift wisdom. That which leads to the state of swift wisdom is called "swift wisdom."
“They conduce to keen wisdom”: what is keen wisdom?
It is called keen wisdom because it swiftly cuts off defilements.
It is called keen wisdom because one does not tolerate an arisen thought of sensual desire, but abandons it, dispels it, brings it to an end, and causes it to vanish.
One does not tolerate a thought of ill will that has arisen; one abandons it, dispels it, brings it to an end, and causes it to cease—this is sharp wisdom.

One does not tolerate a thought of cruelty that has arisen … [and so on] … one does not tolerate evil, unwholesome states as they arise; one abandons them, dispels them, brings them to an end, and causes them to cease—this is sharp wisdom.
She does not tolerate arisen lust; she abandons it, dispels it, brings it to an end, and makes it non-existent—thus she is one of keen wisdom.
[Likewise] arisen hatred...
arisen delusion...
arisen anger … arisen resentment … slander …
...vanity... envy...
stinginess...
Deceit … guile … obstinacy …
... aggression ...
conceit ...
overweening pride ...
Arrogance … negligence … all defilements …

She does not tolerate, abandons, dispels, brings to an end, and causes the disappearance of all misconduct … all volitional formations … all kamma leading to existence; thus she is one of sharp wisdom.

When, on a single seat, the four noble paths, the four fruits of recluseship, the four analytical insights, and the six direct knowledges are attained, realized, touched, and verified by wisdom— this is sharp wisdom.
That which leads to the state of having sharp wisdom—
this is called sharp wisdom.
"They conduce to penetrative wisdom. What is penetrative wisdom?
Here, a certain person is full of agitation regarding all conditioned phenomena, full of terror, full of distaste, full of dissatisfaction, and full of lack of delight.
He does not find pleasure in conditioned phenomena; his mind is turned outward.
It pierces and shatters the mass of greed never before pierced and never before shattered—thus it is penetrative wisdom.
It pierces and shatters the mass of hatred never before pierced and never before shattered—thus it is penetrative wisdom.
It pierces and shatters the mass of delusion never before pierced and never before shattered—thus it is penetrative wisdom.
Anger never before pierced, never before shattered … enmity … slander … [and so on] … [as above].
... malice ...
envy ...
avarice ...
Deceit … guile … obstinacy …
...aggression...
pride...
arrogance...
Arrogance … negligence … all defilements …
It is "penetrative wisdom" because it becomes disillusioned with and shatters all misconduct, all volitional formations, and so on, up to all kamma that leads to existence.
They conduce to penetrative wisdom—
this is penetrative wisdom.
These are the sixteen kinds of wisdom.
A person endowed with these sixteen kinds of wisdom has attained the analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā).
3.1.2. Designation of Distinct Persons:
Two persons have attained the analytical knowledges—
One is endowed with prior application; one is not endowed with prior application.
He who is endowed with prior application excels, surpasses, and distinguishes himself by that;
his knowledge breaks forth.
There are two persons who have attained analytical knowledge (*paṭisambhidā*);
both are endowed with prior application (*pubbayoga*), yet one is learned and the other is not learned. He who is learned excels by virtue of that; he is superior and distinguished.
His knowledge breaks forth.
There are two persons who have attained the analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā), both of whom were endowed with prior application and both of whom are learned;
yet one is rich in teaching, while the other is not rich in teaching.
He who is abundant in teaching excels by that quality; he becomes superior and distinguished.
His knowledge breaks forth.
There are two persons who have attained the analytical knowledges (*paṭisambhidā*), both of whom are endowed with past practice, both of whom are learned, and both of whom are abundant in teaching.
One relies on the teacher; one does not rely on the teacher.
He who relies on the teacher excels, surpasses, and becomes distinguished by that means;
his knowledge breaks forth.

There are two persons who have attained analytical knowledge; both are endowed with past application, both are learned, both are frequent in teaching, and both rely on a teacher—one is abundant in dwelling, the other is not abundant in dwelling.
He who is abundant in dwelling is superior by virtue of that; he is more excellent, he is distinguished.
His knowledge breaks forth.

There are two types of persons who have attained analytical insight (*paṭisambhidā*); both are endowed with past application, both are learned, both are frequent in teaching, both are dependent upon a teacher, and both are frequent in dwelling [in meditation].
One is frequent in reflection; the other is not frequent in reflection.
He who is abundant in reflection becomes superior, pre-eminent, and distinguished by that very quality;
his knowledge becomes radiant.

There are two types of persons who have attained the analytical knowledges (*paṭisambhidā*): both are endowed with past practice, both are learned, both are abundant in teaching, both rely upon a teacher, both are abundant in dwelling [in meditation], and both are abundant in reflection.
One has attained the analytical knowledges of one still in training; the other has attained the analytical knowledges of one beyond training.
He who has attained the analytical knowledges of one beyond training is superior, more excellent, and distinguished by that;
his knowledge becomes manifold.
Two persons have attained the analytical knowledges (*paṭisambhidā*); both are endowed with past application; both are learned; both are frequent in teaching;
both are dependent on a teacher; both are frequent in abiding [in meditation]; both are frequent in reflection;

both have attained the analytical knowledges of one beyond training (*asekha*)—one has reached the perfection of a disciple (*sāvakapārami*), while the other has not reached the perfection of a disciple.
One who has attained the perfection of a disciple excels, surpasses, and is distinguished by that [attainment].
His knowledge becomes manifold.
There are two persons who have attained the analytical knowledges (*paṭisambhidā*); both are endowed with past application, both are learned, and both are frequent in teaching.
Both rely on a teacher; both dwell much in meditation; both are much given to reflection;
both have attained the analytical knowledges of one beyond training—one has reached the perfection of a disciple, while the other is a paccekabuddha.
That which is a paccekabuddha is superior to the former, more excellent, and distinguished.
His knowledge breaks forth.
Compared with a paccekabuddha and the world with its devas, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is supreme;

he has attained the analytical knowledges, is skilled in the breaking forth of wisdom, possesses broken-forth knowledge, has acquired the analytical knowledges, has attained the four grounds of self-confidence, and wields the ten powers.
A bull among men, a lion among men...
even those wise khattiyas, wise brahmins, wise householders, and wise ascetics— clever, skilled in the doctrines of others,
like hair-splitting archers who move as if piercing through [targets] with the range of their wisdom— having formulated a question, [approached him].
Having prepared themselves, they approach the Tathāgata and ask about things that are hidden and concealed.
Those questions are answered and resolved by the Blessed One with their underlying reasons explained; they are successfully disposed of before the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One outshines them there, namely through wisdom, as one who has attained the analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) and is supreme.
The Discourse on Great Wisdom is finished.
